question: 1° of latitude is equal to ___ km approximately.
solution:
The correct answer is __**111.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Equator** is an extremely good circle and the circumference of a circle is the same as** 3600, 10 angular **distance is approximately equal to **111km.**
 
• The range is the dimension of distance north or south of the Equator.
 
• These lines are known as parallels. A circle of the range is an imaginary ring linking all points sharing a parallel.
 
• **Traces of latitude,** also called parallels, are imaginary lines that divide the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hipparchus, a Greek astronomer** (a hundred ninety–hundred twenty BC), **became the first to specify the region through the use of range and longitude as coordinates.
 
• It's far measured with one hundred eighty imaginary lines that shape circles around Earth east-west, parallel to the Equator. 
 
• At the equator, an arc-second of longitude approximately equals an **arc-2nd of range**, that is 1/sixtieth of a nautical mile or a hundred and one.**27 feet or 30.87 meters.**
 
• One minute of range equals one nautical mile, which is identical to at least one**.15 land miles (1. Eighty-five km).**
 
• Each minute of the range is in addition divided into **60 seconds (“).**
